text:
Edmonton outplayed Vancouver for most of the night and still lost in overtime. EDM carried a 3.68 to 2.00 edge in expected goals and a 72 to 44 edge in shot attempts, which is why the simulated replays gave the Oilers a 78 percent chance to win. The result went the other way because of the goaltending. Tristan Jarry allowed 4.0 goals more than the 23 shots he faced should have produced, while Kevin Lankinen, at 1.32 below expected, was the lesser problem.

Vancouver got ahead and then padded it in a hurry. Paul Cotter scored shorthanded in the first period, and Marco Rossi made it 2-1 early in the second. Evan Bouchard tied it at 2-2 in the second, but the third period began with three Canucks goals in just over four minutes, from Jonathan Lekkerimäki, Max Sasson and Elias Pettersson on the power play. Only the Pettersson tip-in came on a chance above single digits for the first two.

Edmonton then nearly erased it all. Vasily Podkolzin scored at 8:56 and Bouchard, on a wrist shot that carried a 2 percent chance, scored 24 seconds later. Podkolzin tied it with the extra attacker's power play at 19:17. Bouchard finished with three goals and two assists. In overtime, Cotter took a pass from Sasson and put a backhand away at 1:59, a 42 percent chance that decided it.
